# gitmoap_group_access (Data Source)

Who has access to a group, and why. Lists every live grant that reaches the group — made on it, or inherited from a group above — oldest first, each with its holder, role, expiry, reason and any limit narrowing it. Filter by where the grant was made, by the kind of holder, or by a name fragment. Callers who can see who has access here may read it (Reporters and above with the built-in roles); a public or internal group does not make its access list public.

The token needs `access:read`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "gitmoap_group_by_path" "acme" {
  full_path = "acme"
}

data "gitmoap_group_access" "acme" {
  group_id = data.gitmoap_group_by_path.acme.group_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `group_id` (String) Group ID

### Optional

- `search` (String) A fragment of a username, or of a team's name
- `source` (String) Only grants made here (`direct`), only inherited ones (`inherited`), or both (`all`, the default)
- `subject_kind` (String) Only grants to people, service accounts or teams

### Read-Only

- `advanced_in_use` (Boolean) Whether the organization has given a team access, or defined a custom role or a limit. Until
it has, access is five roles given to people, and the page reads as a members list.
- `entries` (Attributes List) Every grant that reaches here — made here or inherited — oldest first. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--entries))
- `organization_owners` (Attributes) The organization's owners, who reach everything whatever the page lists. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--organization_owners))
- `scope` (Attributes) A group or repository as its access page describes it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scope))

<a id="nestedatt--entries"></a>
### Nested Schema for `entries`

Read-Only:

- `created_at` (String)
- `expires_at` (String)
- `grant_id` (String)
- `granted_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--entries--granted_by))
- `last_exercised_at` (String) When the grant last let somebody do something, to the day. Absent until it has.
- `limited_to` (Attributes List) The limits that take away part of what this grant gives here: set on this group or
repository or one above it, naming the grant's holder, a team the person is on, or everyone
— or every service account, for one. An organization owner is never limited, so their
entries carry none. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--entries--limited_to))
- `reason` (String)
- `role` (Attributes) A role — built in or defined by the organization — with its display name and the built-in rank
it counts as. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--entries--role))
- `source` (Attributes) Where an entry on the access page was granted. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--entries--source))

<a id="nestedatt--entries--granted_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `entries.granted_by`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.


<a id="nestedatt--entries--limited_to"></a>
### Nested Schema for `entries.limited_to`

Read-Only:

- `at` (Attributes) A group or repository, as the access API names one. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--entries--limited_to--at))
- `ceiling` (Attributes) A role — built in or defined by the organization — with its display name and the built-in rank
it counts as. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--entries--limited_to--ceiling))
- `created_at` (String)
- `created_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--entries--limited_to--created_by))
- `limit_id` (String)
- `reason` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--organization_owners"></a>
### Nested Schema for `organization_owners`

Read-Only:

- `count` (Number)
- `listed` (Boolean) Whether their grants appear among the entries. They do not when this group or repository
stops inheriting access, yet the owners reach it all the same.


<a id="nestedatt--scope"></a>
### Nested Schema for `scope`

Read-Only:

- `full_path` (String)
- `id` (String)
- `inherits_access` (Boolean) Whether access granted on the groups above reaches it. When it is `false`, only access
granted here — and the organization's owners — reach it.
- `type` (String)
